title: Tilewise response profiles and SDK spec (WIP)
body:
Status: WIP (brainstorm + lightweight PRD)
Owner: Jordan Li (product-hosted-api)
Collaborators: Samira Ortiz (DX), Evan Patel (serving-runtime), Marta Novak (applied-ml)
Context / why this doc exists
- We keep iterating on incremental/partial streaming and tool calls. Many SDK patterns focus on entire response streams or on fixed partial JSON frames. Teams keep asking for: (1) deterministic partial structured chunks that can be independently consumed, validated and retried; (2) a compact SDK handshake that signals backpressure / priority per chunk; (3) heuristics to split responses into tiles that map to latency/cost budgets.
- This doc explores "tilewise" response profiles: conceptual model where a model response is partitioned into ordered "tiles" (units of progressive fidelity). Tiles can be typed (narrative-text, table, action, tool-proxy), individually validated, and sent over streaming endpoints. The SDK exposes a small contract to receive/ack tiles, request replays, and attach tool-calls to specific tiles.
Executive summary (one paragraph)
- Proposal: a streaming payload contract + minimal SDK handshake that treats partial output as typed tiles. Tiles enable: low-latency usable results, targeted re-run/fallthrough on specific tiles, cheaper caching (tile-level KV), and clearer observability per logical unit. We sketch API surface (transport-agnostic), SDK ergonomics for web and mobile clients, runtime expectations, telemetry signals, and rollout experiment plan.
Goals
- Reduce end-to-end perceived latency for common micro-interactions (summaries, answer-with-sources, step-by-step code) by allowing first useful tile to be surfaced quickly.
- Make tool-calling deterministic and debuggable: attach a tool-call to tile index -> observable binding and replay semantics.
- Keep server-side runtime simple: tiles are a logical framing; runtime can still stream tokens but must emit tile boundaries (metadata).
- Provide clear SDK ergonomics so most client devs can adopt with small code changes.
Non-goals
- Not a replacement for full session compression or long-term transcript storage.
- Not trying to ship a heavy serialization language; keep tile metadata minimal and typed.
Concepts and primitive definitions
- Tile: ordered unit of progressive output. A tile contains: id (string), type (string enum), ordinal (int), content (string or structured payload), optional tool_binding (tool_id + args), checksum (optional).
- Tile profile: hints about expected size, latency priority and cost bucket. Examples: fast-summary (small tokens, high priority), evidence-table (structured, mid priority), long-form (low priority).
- Tile stream: sequence of tiles delivered over streaming path, with markers for start/end and optional tile-level finalization event. Token stream inside a tile may be interleaved with tokens from model, but SDK gets tile boundary events.
API sketches
- HTTP chunked streaming / SSE / websocket all supported. Core contract: every message is either: TILE_START, TILE_CHUNK, TILE_END, TILE_FINAL (finalization + signatures), HEARTBEAT, ERROR. TILE_START contains tile metadata header (id, type, profile).
- Example wire (pseudo):
  {type: "TILE_START", id: "t-0", tile_type: "fast-summary", profile: "summary-compact"}
  {type: "TILE_CHUNK", id: "t-0", text: "Here's a quick summary: "}
  {type: "TILE_END", id: "t-0", tokens: 18}
  {type: "TILE_FINAL", id: "t-0", signature: "..."}
- Tool-binding: tile metadata may include tool_binding: {tool: "search-v1", args_hint: {q: "top-3 sources"}}. Server may call tool automatically or emit a TOOL_TRIGGER event referencing tile id.
SDK ergonomics (developer experience)
- Goal: minimal surface for clients. SDK should expose 3 primary primitives: onTile(callback), requestReplay(tileId), attachTool(tileId, toolDescriptor).
- Web (JS) example:
  const s = client.stream({prompt})
  s.onTile(tile => { switch(tile.type) { case 'fast-summary': showToast(tile.content); break; case 'action': openActionModal(tile.content); break; }} )
  s.requestReplay('t-0') // ask server to re-generate tile 0 (fast path)
- Mobile / offline: allow partial tile caching keyed by (model+prompt-hash+tile-id). Use TTLs per tile profile.
Server runtime expectations and simplifications
- Runtime does not need to synthesize tiles natively; we can mark boundary heuristics (prefix classifier or forced special tokens). Runtime needs to attach minimal header metadata at boundaries.
- Fallback behavior: if client does not understand tiles, we stream entire flattened text as legacy messages (gateway compatibility).
Observability and telemetry
- Tile-level metrics: time_to_first_tile, mean_tile_latency, tile_size_tokens, tile_retry_rate, tile_tool_trigger_rate.
- Expose per-tile traces in Console: allow filtering traces by tile_type and tool_binding.
- Billing implications: option to bill by tile_size_tokens for incremental early tiles vs full token count; ops to run experiments on billing model.
Tool calling and replay semantics
- Tool invocations can be: eager (server triggers tool) or delegated (client triggers). Each invocation references tile_id and returns a tool_response_id.
- Replay semantics: requestReplay(tileId) creates a new partial generation focused only on the tile context (preserving earlier tiles unless tiled seed differs). Server should offer a fast-path variant (lower temperature / constrained decoding) for replays.
Security and safety notes
- Tiles that include tool bindings must be audited: attach provenance header with request id, user id (hashed) and KMS-signed markers.
- Structured tiles (e.g., table of sources) should include normalization guidance to prevent injection (escape sequences, explicit types).
Rollout plan / experiments
- Phase 0 (lab): implement server tile headers + JS SDK in internal sandbox. Run with 10 internal teams. Collect metrics (time_to_first_tile, adoption friction).
- Phase 1 (beta): gated release for selected customers, feature-flagged billing experiments (no billing change initially).
- Phase 2 (GA): finalize SDK contracts, enable tile-level telemetry in Console, document migration guide (legacy streaming -> tilewise).
Open questions and tradeoffs (short list)
- How opinionated should tile profiles be? Offer 4 canonical profiles and let customers add custom profiles?
- How to handle stateful tool calls that depend on multiple tiles? (tool graph vs single tile binding)
- Bandwidth/latency: for very small tiles, overhead of tile headers may be non-trivial. Need compact binary framing for high-throughput scenarios.
- SDK ergonomic differences for mobile vs server-side libs.
Next steps / immediate TODOs
- [ ] Evan: prototype TILE_START/TILE_END markers in the runtime stream (P0).
- [ ] Samira: draft JS SDK onTile API and small demo repo. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/hosted-sdk/pull/412
- [ ] Marta: run two prompt families through tile classifier to propose 4 canonical profiles.
- [ ] Jordan: prepare beta customer brief + migration notes.
References / links
- CONFL-1234: streaming framing decisions (notes)
- JIRA-9876: tilewise experiment tickets
- GH PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/hosted-sdk/pull/412
Notes to reviewers
- This is intentionally lightweight — we want feedback on the conceptual mapping (tile -> tool_bind -> replay) before standardizing shape. Think about your mobile SDKs: will requestReplay be unnatural? Do we need a separate prefetch primitive?
- If you have latency-sensitive demos (search snippets, quick code generation), try to map them to a 1-2 tile design and share telemetry if you can.
